8319.t: From Proto-Hellenic *(s)tégos, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tégos, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg- (“to cover”). Cognate with Latin tego (“to cover”), German Decke (“roof”), English thatch.

8320.t: From Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg- (“to cover, roof”). Cognate with Lithuanian sti̇́egiu (“to thatch, to cover a roof”), Latin tegō (“to cover”), Proto-Germanic *þakjaną (“to cover”).

8353.t: From συλλέγω (sullégō, “to gather, collect”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix).

8310.t: From στρέφω (stréphō, “to twist”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

8383.t: From συν- (sun-, “with, together”) + πίνω (pínō, “to drink”). Compare Ancient Greek ἀναπίνω (anapínō).

8322.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sterg- (literally “to cover, to protect”). Possibly related to Proto-Slavic *sterťi (“to guard”) and Welsh serch (“love, affection”).

8316.t: There are no known cognates. Furnée compares the word with τοπεῖον (topeîon, “rope”).

8312.t: Ultimately from στρέφω (stréphō, “to turn; to rotate”).

8389.t: From συν- (sŭn-, “with, together”) + φύω (phŭ́ō, “to bring forth, to produce”).

8321.t: The entry by Beekes in his Etymological Dictionary of Greek reads: “A full-grade variant of σταφυλή (staphulḗ, “grape”). No further etymology; perhaps Pre-Greek, if the -μ- is interpreted as prenasalization.

8309.t: From the o-grade of στρέφω (stréphō, “to twist, turn”) + -ος (-os).
